title: Induction step for topology-comparison vanishing
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a category small in a universe containing the sites and coefficients [def-weil-size-convention], endowed with two site structures $\tau$ and $\tau'$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] such that every $\tau'$-covering is a $\tau$-covering. For $X\in\mathcal C$, let $\mathcal C_\tau/X$ and $\mathcal C_{\tau'}/X$ be the slice sites: their objects are arrows $U\to X$, their morphisms are commutative triangles, and their coverings are those whose underlying families cover $U$ in the respective topology. Let $\epsilon_X:\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C_\tau/X)\to\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C_{\tau'}/X)$ be the comparison geometric morphism [def-trf-geometric-morphism] with direct image the identity on underlying presheaves and inverse image $\tau$ sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. For $f:X\to Y$ write $f_{\tau'}$ for the relocalization morphism of slice topoi whose inverse image sends $H$ to $(U\to X)\mapsto H(U\to X\to Y)$. Higher direct images below mean the ordinary right derived functors on abelian sheaves, computed using injective resolutions. Suppose that a class $\mathcal P$ of morphisms and full subcategories $\mathcal A'_X\subset\mathrm{Ab}(\mathcal C_{\tau'}/X)$ have the following properties. Each $\mathcal A'_X$ contains zero and is closed under isomorphisms, kernels and cokernels of morphisms between its objects, and extensions (the weak Serre condition). Assume in addition:

(1) For $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathcal P$ and any $Y'\to Y$, the fibre product $X\times_Y Y'$ exists and $X\times_Y Y'\to Y'$ lies in $\mathcal P$.

(2) For every $f:X\to Y$, one has $f_{\tau'}^{-1}(\mathcal A'_Y)\subset\mathcal A'_X$.

(3) Every $H'\in\mathcal A'_X$ already satisfies the $\tau$ sheaf condition on $\mathcal C/X$.

(4) For $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathcal P$, $H'\in\mathcal A'_X$ and every $i\geq0$, one has $R^if_{\tau',*}H'\in\mathcal A'_Y$.

(5) Every $\tau$-covering $\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ has a refinement $\{W_{jk}\to U\}_{j\in J,k\in K_j}$ obtained by composing a $\tau'$-covering $\{V_j\to U\}_{j\in J}$, singleton $\tau$-coverings $\{W_j\to V_j\}$ with morphisms in $\mathcal P$, and $\tau'$-coverings $\{W_{jk}\to W_j\}_{k\in K_j}$. Refinement means that every composite factors through some $U_i\to U$.

For each $X$, let $\mathcal A_X$ be the full subcategory of $\mathrm{Ab}(\mathcal C_\tau/X)$ consisting of sheaves isomorphic to $\epsilon_X^{-1}H'$ for $H'\in\mathcal A'_X$. For $r\geq0$, let $(V_r)$ mean $R^i\epsilon_{X,*}H=0$ for every $X$, $H\in\mathcal A_X$ and $1\leq i\leq r$. Then $(V_r)$ implies $(V_{r+1})$.

proof.text: Fix $r\geq0$ and assume $(V_r)$. If $F\in\mathcal A_Y$, choose $F'\in\mathcal A'_Y$ with $F=\epsilon_Y^{-1}F'$. Since $F'$ already is a $\tau$-sheaf, sheafification fixes it and $\epsilon_{Y,*}F=F'$. For $g:Z\to Y$, the presheaf underlying $g_{\tau'}^{-1}F'$ is its sectionwise restriction. By assumption (2) this restriction is in $\mathcal A'_Z$, hence already a $\tau$-sheaf by (3). Consequently $g_\tau^{-1}F=\epsilon_Z^{-1}g_{\tau'}^{-1}F'\in\mathcal A_Z$ and $\epsilon_{Z,*}g_\tau^{-1}F=g_{\tau'}^{-1}\epsilon_{Y,*}F$. The comparison inverse image is exact because it is abelian sheafification.

source.place: Tag 0EZ9, lemma-A, its proof; section-compare-general, equation-commutative-epsilon.

proof.text: For $F\in\mathcal A_Y$, the sheaf $R^{r+1}\epsilon_{Y,*}F$ is the $\tau'$-sheafification of $U\mapsto H^{r+1}_\tau(U,F)$. The localization isomorphism identifies this with cohomology on the slice over $U$ with coefficient $F|_U\in\mathcal A_U$ from Step 1. Thus it suffices to show that every such class becomes zero on a $\tau'$-cover of $U$: any map from a locally zero presheaf to a sheaf is zero by sheaf separation; the sheafification adjunction then forces its sheafification to be zero. We may rename $U$ as $Y$ and $F|_U$ as $F$; further $\tau'$-cover replacements can be composed.

source.place: Tag 0EZE, first paragraph; Tag 072W, lemma-higher-direct-images; Tag 03F3, lemma-cohomology-of-open.

proof.text: Every positive-degree cohomology class on either slice site is locally zero. Indeed, represent it by a cocycle $s\in I^q(U)$ in an injective resolution of its sheaf, $q>0$. Exactness of the resolution makes $I^{q-1}\to\ker(d^q)$ an epimorphism. Kernels are sectionwise; local surjectivity supplies a covering and sections $t_i$ with $d t_i=s|_{U_i}$, so the restricted classes vanish. Apply this with $q=r+1$ to $\xi\in H^{r+1}_\tau(Y,F)$, obtaining a $\tau$-cover killing $\xi$.

source.place: Tag 01FW, lemma-kill-cohomology-class-on-covering, proof; used in Tag 0EZE, second paragraph.

proof.text: Refine that cover as in assumption (5): $V_j\to Y$ is a $\tau'$-cover, $f_j:W_j\to V_j$ lies in $\mathcal P$ and is a singleton $\tau$-cover, and $W_{jk}\to W_j$ is a $\tau'$-cover. Each composite $W_{jk}\to Y$ factors through an original member, so $\xi|_{W_{jk}}=0$. By Step 2 it is enough to work over one $V_j$. Rename it $Y$, rename $W_j$ as $T$, and write $f:T\to Y$. The resulting problem has $F\in\mathcal A_Y$, $f\in\mathcal P$ a singleton $\tau$-cover, and $\xi|_T$ killed by a $\tau'$-cover of $T$.

source.place: Tag 0EZE, refinement paragraph and first reduced problem.

proof.text: The next-degree comparison gives a unique $\theta\in H^{r+1}_{\tau'}(T,\epsilon_{T,*}f_\tau^{-1}F)$ mapping to $\xi|_T$. On $T\times_YT$, the images of the two pullbacks of $\theta$ are equal: both are the pullback of $\xi$ along the same composite to $Y$. Restriction naturality and injectivity of that same comparison on $T\times_YT$ therefore give $\operatorname{pr}_1^*\theta=\operatorname{pr}_2^*\theta$. This fibre product exists by (1), and its restricted coefficient lies in the required class by Step 1.

Put $F'=\epsilon_{Y,*}F\in\mathcal A'_Y$; Step 1 identifies the coefficient of $\theta$ with $F'|_T$. The equalizer-class lemma, with $q=r+1\geq1$, supplies a $\tau'$-cover $Y_a\to Y$ on which $\theta$ becomes zero on $T\times_YY_a$. Its comparison image is the restriction of $\xi$ there. The base changed $f$ remains in $\mathcal P$ by (1) and remains a singleton $\tau$-cover by the site axiom. After this allowed replacement we have reduced to $\xi|_T=0$.

source.place: Tag 0EZE, end of the theta paragraph; Tag 0EZD, lemma-make-class-zero-general.

proof.text: Let $E=f_\tau^{-1}F$ and $D=Rf_{\tau,*}E$. Derived composition gives $R\Gamma_\tau(Y,D)=R\Gamma_\tau(T,E)$ and identifies the map induced by the adjunction unit $F\to D$ with cohomology restriction along $f$. Indeed at the underived level both maps send a section to its restriction to the slice over $T$, and the canonical resolution comparison in the composition theorem derives that same map. Thus $\xi$ maps to zero in $H^{r+1}_\tau(Y,D)$. Here abelian sheaves are constant-$\mathbb Z$ modules with their unique integer action; apply the ringed-topos composition theorem with these constant ring sheaves and the map to the punctual topos.

source.place: Tag 0EZE, paragraph beginning with the map to Rf_*; Tag 0D6H, lemma-Leray-unbounded.

proof.text: Set $D_{\leq r}=\tau_{\leq r}D$ and $Q=\tau_{\geq r+1}D$. The standard truncation triangle is $D_{\leq r}\to D\to Q\to$. Represent $Q$ by a complex zero below $r+1$, resolve it by injectives zero below the same bound, and compute derived sections on that resolution. The resulting section complex is zero below $r+1$, so $H^r_\tau(Y,Q)=0$. The long exact sequence of the truncation triangle therefore makes $H^{r+1}_\tau(Y,D_{\leq r})\to H^{r+1}_\tau(Y,D)$ injective. The unit $F\to D$ factors through $D_{\leq r}$ by t-structure orthogonality, since $F$ is in degree zero and $r\geq0$. Consequently $\xi$ maps to zero already in $H^{r+1}_\tau(Y,D_{\leq r})$.

source.place: Tag 0EZE, “simple argument” with the truncation triangle; Derived Categories Tag 08J5, remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle.

proof.text: Put $D'=Rf_{\tau',*}f_{\tau'}^{-1}F'$ and $K=\tau_{\leq r}D'$. By Step 1, $f_{\tau'}^{-1}F'=\epsilon_{T,*}E$. Use the adjoint comparison $b_E:\epsilon_Y^{-1}D'\to D$ specified by the truncated-direct-image lemma. Exactness of $\epsilon_Y^{-1}$ makes its cohomology map in degree $i\leq r$ the $\tau$-sheafification of that lemma's canonical isomorphism $R^if_{\tau',*}\epsilon_{T,*}E\to\epsilon_{Y,*}R^if_{\tau,*}E$. Sheafification of the right-hand side is $R^if_{\tau,*}E$. Hence truncating $b_E$ gives an isomorphism $\beta:\epsilon_Y^{-1}K\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{\leq r}$, including negative degrees, where both sides vanish.

source.place: Tag 0EZE, comparison of truncated derived direct images, applying Tag 0EZA.

proof.text: The augmentation $u':F'\to K$ is the factorization through $\tau_{\leq r}$ of the derived unit for $f_{\tau'}$. Under $\epsilon_Y^{-1}F'=F$, the composite $\beta\circ\epsilon_Y^{-1}u'$ is the factored unit $F\to D_{\leq r}$ of Step 8. To check the map, before truncating compose $F'\to Rf_{\tau',*}f_{\tau'}^{-1}F'$ with $a_E$ from the comparison lemma. The composite is $F'\to R\epsilon_{Y,*}F\to R\epsilon_{Y,*}D$: both are the unit for the composite adjunction, since $\epsilon_{T,*}f_\tau^{-1}F=f_{\tau'}^{-1}\epsilon_{Y,*}F$. Taking the $\epsilon_Y$ adjoint cancels its unit and counit and yields the unit for $f_\tau$. Functorial truncation preserves this equality.

source.place: Tag 0EZE, comparison map induced by adjunction and the two augmented triangles.

proof.text: Choose the cone triangle $F'\xrightarrow{u'}K\to L\to F'[1]$. The degree-zero map is $F'\to f_{\tau',*}f_{\tau'}^{-1}F'$, which on an object $U\to Y$ is restriction $F'(U)\to F'(U\times_YT)$. It is injective since $F'$ is a $\tau$-sheaf and $U\times_YT\to U$ is a singleton $\tau$-cover. From the triangle's cohomology sequence, $L$ has cohomology only in $[0,r]$, with $\mathcal H^0(L)=\operatorname{coker}(F'\to f_{\tau',*}f_{\tau'}^{-1}F')$ and $\mathcal H^i(L)=R^if_{\tau',*}f_{\tau'}^{-1}F'$ for $1\leq i\leq r$. Assumptions (2),(4) and weak Serre closure under cokernels put all these sheaves in $\mathcal A'_Y$. This includes $r=0$.

source.place: Tag 0EZE, cone L and its cohomology sheaves; assumptions of Tag 0EZ3.

proof.text: Pull back the cone triangle by exact $\epsilon_Y^{-1}$, using $\beta$ and the augmentation equality in Step 10. This gives $F\to D_{\leq r}\to\epsilon_Y^{-1}L\to F[1]$. Derived sections preserve distinguished triangles, so exactness and Step 8 provide $\xi'\in H^r_\tau(Y,\epsilon_Y^{-1}L)$ whose boundary is $\xi$. The truncated-cohomology comparison applies to $L$ by Step 11, and lifts $\xi'$ to $\eta\in H^r_{\tau'}(Y,L)$.

source.place: Tag 0EZE, pullback triangle and lift of xi prime using Tag 0EZB.

proof.text: Let $\zeta=\partial\eta\in H^{r+1}_{\tau'}(Y,F')$. Naturality of the long exact sequence, for the comparison from the original cone triangle to its pulled-back triangle followed by derived sections, gives $\epsilon_Y^*(\partial\eta)=\partial(\epsilon_Y^*\eta)=\partial\xi'=\xi$. This uses the actual canonical comparison from Step 12; an arbitrary isomorphism of groups would not suffice. By the positive-degree local-vanishing argument in Step 3, $\zeta$ is killed by a $\tau'$-cover. Restricting its comparison image shows that $\xi$ is killed by the same cover. Composing all earlier $\tau'$-covers proves the local assertion in Step 2. Thus $R^{r+1}\epsilon_{Y,*}F=0$; together with $(V_r)$ this is $(V_{r+1})$.

source.place: Tag 0EZE, final boundary and locality paragraph; Tag 01FW.

split_report.summary: Expanded the Tag 0EZE induction proof in thirteen steps, keeping all five source hypotheses and making the classes, slice sites and refinement precise. Reused existing general-site and derived-category tools. Added four statement-only lemmas for Tags 0EZA--0EZD after DAG, blueprint, Lean and logged Mathlib searches. Wrote out the local-cocycle argument, truncation injection, augmentation equality, cone cohomology including r=0, and naturality of the final boundary. No statement dispute or route change.
split_report.blueprint: The comparison-vanishing induction branch beneath lem-trf-local-term-locality, as specified by the inherited from.place and via chain; source Tag 0EZE is expanded rather than replaced. The ancestor blueprint uses specialization in its (1)--(2) proof.

tool_uses.why: General-site sheafified cohomology formula used to test comparison direct-image vanishing; no such formula belongs to the curve-local-term unit.
General-site localization identifies cohomology on a slice with cohomology over its final object, needed in the source reduction.
Canonical general ringed-topos Leray/composition identification, specialized to integer modules, identifies the unit map with cohomology restriction.
The explicit lower-bound-preserving injective resolution proves the short connective hypercohomology vanishing used by the truncation argument.
General derived-functor preservation of triangles, applied to the sections functor in the source triangle argument.
